newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QBE sees 10-20 pct 96/97 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QBE sees 10-20 pct 96/97 profit rise.

text.p: QBE Insurances Ltd said on Monday it expects to achieve an increase of 10 to 20 percent in 1996/97 net profit.

QBE managing director John Cloney said the profit forecast was based on the company's individual accounting policy which did not include unrealised gains on investments and was closer to a historical costs basis.
"We expect next year an increase of 10 to 20 percent," Cloney told reporters.

"We are fairly confident that we will again next year (1996/97) be able to increase our profits and therefore increase our dividend," Cloney said. QBE earlier announced a net profit of A$147.3 million, after unrealised gains on investments of A$40.2 million, compared with A$82.5 million in 1994/95.
The company's annual dividend payout rose 16.3 percent to A$68.5 million and this was the 29th consecutive rise in interim and final dividends.
"We are not saying we are going to go through the roof and I wouldn't want to give that impression but we do feel confident about our next 12 months," he said.

The general insurance and reinsurance company said that, based on its preferred measure, 1995/96 net profit rose 15.1 percent to A$123.3 million, while the industry-recognised net profit rose 78.5 percent to A$147.3 million.
"I prefer not to talk about profits but we would say that next year we would increase our profits by between 10 and 20 percent," Cloney said.
